title: Example: notification bell count does not update in a background tab
description: Demonstration record showing how a defect is written up. It is not a real defect: polling deliberately pauses while a tab is hidden and resumes when the tab becomes visible.
steps:
1. Sign in as an administrator.
2. Switch to another tab for two minutes while a patient submits a request.
3. Return to the Vitaliq tab.
expected: The count updates as soon as the tab is visible again.
resolution: Demonstration record. Behaviour is by design and documented in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

title: Example: request for SMS notification when results are released
description: Demonstration record of an enhancement request raised from community feedback. No SMS gateway is configured in this project.
steps:
1. Release a result for a patient.
2. Check the patient's phone.
expected: An SMS is sent (if an SMS gateway were configured).
actual: Only an in-app notification is created.

title: Catalogue sync silently skipped 5 test cases with duplicate codes
description: The regex cases for the 'required field' rule and the manual testing-request cases both used the TC-REQ- prefix. QaService::syncCatalogue() skips codes that already exist, so five manual cases (TC-REQ-001 to TC-REQ-005) were never loaded and no error was shown.
steps:
1. Run php bin/seed.php on an empty database.
2. Compare the seeder's reported case count with the number of entries in database/qa/regex-cases.json and manual-cases.json.
expected: 151 cases loaded (115 regex + 36 manual), or an error naming the duplicate code.
actual: 146 cases loaded; the duplicates were dropped without any message.
resolution: Renamed the required-field regex cases to TC-RQD-nnn and made syncCatalogue() throw on a repeated code within the catalogue files. Covered by tests/Integration/QaLabTest::testDuplicateCaseCodeInCatalogueIsAnError.

title: Ct value rule accepted 45.1–45.9 although the limit is 45
description: The ct_value pattern ^(?:[0-9]|[1-3][0-9]|4[0-5])(?:\.[0-9])?$ allows a decimal after 45, so 45.9 passed validation. The test_results table has CHECK (ct_value <= 45), so saving such a result would have failed with a database error instead of a field message.
steps:
1. Run the regex suite (php bin/qa.php run).
2. Look at case TC-CT-004 (input 45.9, expected Rejected).
expected: 45.9 is rejected with 'Ct value is not in the expected format'.
actual: Regex suite run #1 recorded 'Accepted by the validator'.
resolution: Pattern changed to ^(?:(?:[0-9]|[1-3][0-9]|4[0-4])(?:\.[0-9])?|45(?:\.0)?)$. TC-CT-004 passes in the next run; unit test RulesTest covers 45, 45.0 and 45.9.

title: Pages widened beyond the viewport at 375 px
description: On /community the topic tabs, and on /patient long references, made grid columns wider than the screen because grid items default to min-width:auto. The layout viewport grew to 453 px (community) and 383 px (patient dashboard), causing horizontal scrolling on phones.
steps:
1. Open /community in a 375 px wide mobile viewport.
2. Compare document.documentElement.scrollWidth with the viewport width.
expected: Document width equals 375 px; wide content scrolls inside its own container.
actual: Document width 453 px; the whole page scrolled sideways.
resolution: Added min-width:0 to grid children (.split, .grid-2, .hero__grid, .form-grid, .footer-grid, .app-shell) and stacked table labels above values below 30 rem. Re-measured 14 pages at 375 px: all equal to the viewport (TC-UI-001).

title: Stacked table cells split multi-line content into the label column
description:
In the small-screen table layout each cell was a two-column grid, so a
and the text after it became separate grid items. The second line (e.g. the patient's mobile number on the phlebotomist task list) appeared under the label column, and status pills stretched to full width.
steps:
1. Sign in as a phlebotomist with an open collection.
2. View /staff below 1024 px wide.
expected: Each value block stays to the right of (or under) its label.
actual: '+91 …' and address lines were displaced into the label column.
resolution: Stacked cells now use block layout with an absolutely positioned label (labels above values on phones).

title: Mobile menu button shown on desktop and navigation crowded at 1024 px
description: `.btn { display:inline-flex }` appears later in the stylesheet than `.nav-toggle { display:none }` with equal specificity, so the Menu button was always visible. At 1024 px the full navigation also wrapped 'COVID-19' and 'Sign in' onto two lines.
expected: Either the full navigation or the Menu button, not both; no wrapped link text.
actual: Both were visible and several links wrapped.
resolution: Scoped the rule to .masthead .nav-toggle, set nav links to nowrap and moved the collapse breakpoint to 75 rem.

title: Phlebotomist 'Recently collected' list showed the oldest collections first
description: The completed-collections query reused the open-task ordering (preferred date ascending), so a sample collected minutes earlier did not appear at the top, and reassigned requests could appear twice.
steps:
1. Sign in as Ramesh Kumar.
2. Record a collection.
3. Look at 'Recently collected'.
expected: The collection just recorded is first.
actual: The list started with collections from August.
resolution: Completed list now queries sample_collections for the phlebotomist ordered by collected_at descending.

title: Text contrast below WCAG AA for badges and sidebar labels
description: Lighthouse on /admin reported: white on coral notification badge 4.2:1, --ink-3 sidebar section labels on the tinted sidebar 4.22:1. A follow-up calculation found teal status text on its wash at 4.12:1.
steps:
1. Sign in as admin.
2. Run a Lighthouse accessibility audit on /admin.
resolution: Badge uses --coral-text (6.26:1), --ink-3 darkened to #5f6b67 (>= 4.64:1 on every background), teal status text uses --teal-text #2f6a66 (5.29:1). Lighthouse accessibility 100 on /admin, /admin/reports, /admin/requests/{id}, /qa, /qa/cases.

title: Wordmark link name did not contain its visible text (WCAG 2.5.3)
description: The header wordmark had aria-label="Vitaliq home" while showing 'Vitaliq — Health data, made meaningful.' at wide widths, so voice-control users saying the visible words could not activate it.
steps: 1. Run Lighthouse on /statistics at desktop width.
resolution: Removed the aria-label; the visible text is the accessible name. Lighthouse re-run: 0 failed audits.

title: Platform figures note broke into columns
description: The note under the homepage figures used display:flex, so each text node and the link became separate flex items and the sentence was laid out as narrow columns.
steps: 1. Open / and scroll to the three platform figures.
expected: One readable sentence with an inline link.
resolution: Note is now a block with an absolutely positioned marker.

title: Registration had no rate limit
description: POST /register accepted unlimited attempts per connection, allowing scripted account creation and enumeration of registered emails and mobile numbers through the duplicate messages.
steps: 1. Submit /register repeatedly from one connection with different or already-registered details.
expected: Attempts beyond a reasonable number are refused.
resolution: 10 attempts per hour per connection (failed attempts count); 429 response. Covered by AbuseLimitsTest.

title: Anonymous test requests had no rate limit
description: POST /test/new accepted unlimited submissions per connection, so the admin queue and notifications could be flooded.
steps: 1. Submit /test/new repeatedly with fresh form tokens from one connection.
expected: Submissions beyond a reasonable number are refused.
resolution: 10 submissions per hour per connection; replays of an accepted form still return its confirmation. Covered by AbuseLimitsTest.

title: PHP runtime vulnerable to CVE-2026-109618/109619
description: The local runtime was PHP 8.4.25; the critical RCE fixes (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w, GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp) ship in 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12. composer.json allowed any PHP >= 8.2.
steps:
1. php -v
2. Compare with the fixed releases.
expected: A fixed PHP release, enforced at install time.
actual: 8.4.25, and nothing prevented installing on a vulnerable PHP.
resolution: Runtime upgraded to 8.4.27 (SHA-256 verified); Composer platform constraint and bin/check-runtime.php added. Covered by RuntimeCheckTest.
